# NW(23) audit — the no-Terrarium test that never ran (2026-11-20)

Owner report after the single-source build: problem 1 (elevated
teleported chunk) and problem 3 (slow coastline) still present;
problem 2 (floating river water) not reported. Save audited:
seed 6769378560502775985; Gandikota 3,197 chunks + Juhu 228.

## Verdict up front

**NW(23) was generated by the previous two-book (hybrid) build,
not by the single-source build.** The save contains terrain
built from Terrarium tiles at BOTH test sites, and the current
source provably cannot produce Terrarium terrain (dataset
classes deleted, no Terrarium URL/fetch anywhere in src/ —
grep-verified; the only elevation fetch is
MapterhornTiles.fetchTile256). So problems 1 and 3 in NW(23)
are the hybrid's known diseases (see SINGLE_ELEVATION_SOURCE.md:
"terrain z15: Mapterhorn-first, Terrarium fallback per tile...
coasts fetched 2 sources x up to 7 zooms (slow)"). The
single-source fix has therefore never actually been tested.
Most likely cause: `gradle jarJar` not re-run, or the old jar
left in the mods folder. Owner's latest.log settles it in one
grep: any `s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod` traffic or
non-Mapterhorn ELEV SRC lines = old jar.

## Proof (save forensics, harness-verified)

Method: per-column saved surface Y vs live-fetched tiles
(Mapterhorn via the mod's own MapterhornTiles; Terrarium via
the public S3 tiles), block->geo through the verified Dymaxion
port, surface Y = 63 + elevation (identity below 1000 m).

- 822 of 823 fittable full chunks match **Mapterhorn z15** to a
  median offset of ~+0.15 blocks. The current pipeline, when it
  runs, is exact.
- The ONE exception is the owner's elevated chunk:
  **(637300,-109800)** at Gandikota (one chunk NE of the NW(20)
  fossil point; the NW(20) chunk itself is healthy in NW(23)).
  +5.0..+5.5 median cliff on ALL FOUR borders, flat terracotta
  cap, biome `badlands` amid `savanna` neighbours. Its columns
  match the **Terrarium** z15 tile: offset +0.35, shape RMSE
  0.37 (vs Mapterhorn: +5.3). It matches neither Mapterhorn
  z14 (+4.7) nor z11 (shape 0.8) — a pure wrong-book chunk,
  born in the first generation burst (lowest LastUpdate in the
  cluster; no buried old surface — born wrong, not raised).
  Its badlands biome is the separate ESA-cold fallback fossil
  (assignBiomes used non-blocking getClass; ROCKY soil
  fallback), same cold-start minute.
- Juhu: at least 5-6 of the 26 full chunks are likewise
  Terrarium-born (offset ~0.0 vs Terrarium, +2.5..+3.0 vs
  Mapterhorn). Invisible in game because flat city coast: all
  local chunks share the wrong book, so no cliff — the ground
  is simply ~3 blocks higher than the new build would make it.
- A stale-disk-tile explanation was tested and REJECTED: the
  spike guard accepts both Terrarium tiles (56 repairs vs
  3,277 quarantine at Gandikota; 0 at Juhu — simulated with
  the real guard code), so a poisoned PNG would be served to
  every chunk of its tile in every session — but the lid's
  tile-mates are Mapterhorn-born. Only a live per-tile
  fallback (hybrid behaviour) fits one wrong chunk among
  right ones. The disk hole is real, though — closed anyway
  (below).

## Problem 3 (slow coast) — real in BOTH builds

Only 26 of 228 Juhu chunks reached `full`; 202 never passed
`structure_starts` (Gandikota: 36% full). The generation
pipeline parks its few worker threads in stacked bounded
waits, all still present in current code: COAST WAIT up to
10 s per coastal chunk behind one slow public-Overpass fetch
(20 s HTTP timeout), ESA WAIT up to 5 s, elevation getTile
3 s timeouts on a 2-4 thread pool, structure waits. Cold
coast = queue collapse. This needed fixing regardless of
which jar ran.

## Fixes applied (this session, parse-clean JDK17)

1. **Disk cache folder `tiles/mapterhorn-v1` -> `mapterhorn-v2`**
   (TerraDensityFunctions). The PNG encoding is identical for
   both books, so a cached tile carries no proof of origin;
   the folder name is the only source marker. No tile written
   by any older build can ever be read again.
2. **Elevation readiness gate** (`fillFromNoise` ->
   `TerraDensityFunctions.awaitTilesForChunk`, 15 s bounded):
   terrain generation now waits until the terrain-zoom tiles
   covering the chunk (+24-block border) are resident instead
   of classifying from the parent/bathymetry fallback ladder
   when a fetch misses getTile's 3 s window. Expired deadline
   = generate anyway + `ELEV NOT READY [cx,cz]` WARN naming
   the chunk. Supporting changes: getTile no longer drops the
   pending entry on timeout (duplicate-download race), fetch
   failures are timestamped (tileFailedAt, 30 s negative
   cache respected by the gate), tile download pool 2-4 -> 4-8
   threads.
3. **COAST WAIT 10 s -> 3 s** (TerraChunkGenerator). The fetch
   now starts at /tpll warm-up / first-chunk prefetch, before
   terrain generation; 3 s gives the shared fetch its chance
   without letting one slow Overpass tile stall the coast.
4. **ESA BIOME WAIT** (`assignBiomes`, 6 s bounded): biome
   classification no longer fossilises on a cold WorldCover
   tile (the savanna->badlands fossil); logs
   `ESA BIOME WAIT [cx,cz] waited=.. loaded=..`.

## NW(23) repair

`/home/user/newworld23_fixed.zip` — identical world with chunk
(637300,-109800) removed from region + entities files (all
other 1,023 chunk payloads byte-identical, verified). It
regenerates on next visit with whatever jar is running. The
Terrarium-born Juhu chunks were left: uniform ~+3, no seams,
invisible; they change only if deleted/regenerated.
